subject: Re: Dedicated capacity terms & start schedule — Skyforge
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@skyforge.ai>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask + timelines / pricing guardrails

Marcus —

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. Were getting internal alignment around a Dedicated deployment and trying to nail down the commercial shape before our exec sync. Quick summary of our ask:

- Target GPU pool: 24 A100-equivalent GPUs (mix of A100 and upcoming H100 nodes)
- Expected steady-state: 400 requests/sec (avg payloads) with spikes to ~750 rps
- Compliance: SOC 2 + EU data residency for a subset of requests
- Preferred start: capacity available by 2026-03-15, full traffic by 2026-04-01

Were running an internal model on projected spend and would like pricing options for 12/24/36 month reserved commits, with suggested discounts and a recommended ramp schedule (we want to avoid paying for idle capacity early but need throughput guarantees once live). Also: please call out any minimum throughput SLAs and the earliest possible capacity start date.

I attached our RFC (Skyforge_RFC_requirements.pdf). Can you send a counterproposal with assumptions?

Cheers,
Elena
VP Product, Skyforge AI
Attach: Skyforge_RFC_requirements.pdf (PDF)
From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@skyforge.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Feb 2026 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask + timelines / pricing guardrails

Elena —

Thanks for the clear RFC and the timelines. We can absolutely size for the throughput you described. Quick high level:

- We can provision a 24-GPU pool and guarantee 95th pct token latency targets for your steady-state throughput, with burst headroom for peak windows.
- Start date: we can carve capacity as early as 2026-03-08 for onboarding validation; full capacity by 2026-03-22 with a staged ramp.
- Pricing: Ill attach a fidelity spreadsheet with 12/24/36 month commit figures and suggested discounts tied to ramp milestones.

Ill loop in Laura for commercial & legal items (SLA guardrails and contract cadence). Expect a formal counterproposal and a proposed ramp cadence by EOD Wednesday.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Feb 2026 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Pricing inputs for Skyforge (24 GPU pool)

Team —

Reviewed Elenas RFC. Commercial notes for the counterproposal:

- Discounting: baseline list multiplied by commit length: 12mo = 0% baseline discount; 24mo = -18% list; 36mo = -28% list. We can consider an additional ~5% early-pay incentive for pre-funded commits.
- Ramp schedule options: A (fast) 3-week ramp to full (recommended for customers confident in traffic), B (staggered) 8-week ramp with checkpoints tied to utilization (useful if they want to spread cost). Discounts tied to utilization: if theyre below 50% utilization at the 60-day check, price adjustment clause triggers.
- Throughput SLA: guarantee of 99.5% availability for the Dedicated pool; throughput SLOs for model-level 95th pct latencies will be in the SLO table depending on model family. We shouldnt promise absolute rps headcounts; instead commit to percent-of-pool capacity for their workload profile.

Karthik, can you confirm the earliest hard start date we can operationalize for a 24-GPU carve? Also add any considerations about mixed GPU fleets (A100/H100) and perf parity.

Laura
Head of Commercials — Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Feb 2026 14:45:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Pricing inputs for Skyforge (24 GPU pool)

Laura / Marcus —

Operational constraints:
- Earliest carve date for a homogeneous A100 pool (24x) is 2026-03-10 if we prioritize their build; mixed pool (12 A100 + 12 H100) we can start earlier, 2026-03-01, but H100 availability depends on partner inventory.
- Perf note: H100 nodes reduce token latencies by ~18% on their current model family but introduce variance across nodes; recommend pinning model variant per node type or using routing policy to send sensitive low-latency traffic to H100 subset.
- Autoscaling: we can configure burst capacity (on-host spare GPUs) for short-term peaks—this will be priced as on-demand compute above the reserved commit.

Ill prepare a small table for the pricing sheet that maps commit length -> discount -> ramp milestones -> utilization measurement points.

- Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Elena Torres <elena@skyforge.ai>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@skyforge.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask + timelines / pricing guardrails

Marcus —

Appreciate the quick turn. A few clarifying questions after reading your internal notes:

1) Were leaning toward a 24-month commit but would like a phased ramp: 30% capacity for first 6 weeks, 65% for next 6 weeks, then full. Can you map discounts to that staged ramp (i.e., larger initial discount if we front-load a bigger initial commit)?
2) Start date: wed prefer 2026-03-08 onboarding start. You mentioned mixed pools might be earlier; open to that if its materially earlier.
3) SLA language: we need a clear remedy for missed throughput SLOs (service credits). Can we see sample SLA language?

Were also evaluating a 36-month path if the economics improve materially — what threshold would you need for more aggressive discounts?

Thanks — will aim to review your spreadsheet tomorrow.

Elena
From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@skyforge.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask + timelines / pricing guardrails

Elena —

Thanks — attached is a counterproposal (MA_proposal_Skyforge_v1.docx) and a pricing workbook (redwood_dedicated_pricing_v3.xlsx). Highlights: 

- 24-month recommended path (balanced): 18% baseline discount off list. Structured further as:
  - Ramp plan (phased): Week 0-6 = 30% pool; Week 7-12 = 65% pool; Week 13+ = 100% pool. If you elect to pre-fund the first 6 weeks wed propose an additional 4% off the 24mo pricing.
  - Alternative 36mo aggressive path: 32% baseline discount with 3% additional early-pay incentive (total ~35%). Requires minimum annualized commit equal to the 24mo baseline.
- Start dates: we can guarantee onboarding carve on 2026-03-01 for a mixed pool (12 A100/12 H100); homogeneous A100 target 2026-03-12. Youre within your 2026-03-15 target either way.
- Throughput/SLOs: we included sample SLA language in the MA: service credits tiered by severity (1% credit for single-day missed throughput SLO; up to 10% for sustained outages >72 hours). We measured SLOs against the profiled model traces you provided.
- Utilization guardrail: two measurement checkpoints at day 45 and day 90. If utilization <50% at day 90, a remediation conversation occurs; we can agree to a one-time adjustment to the next billing period or a reduced committed baseline.

Next steps:
- If that commercial structure looks reasonable, well prepare a redline-friendly MA and propose a DocuSign path.
- If you want us to tighten latency SLOs for specific endpoints, Karthik can produce perf runs on H100 vs A100 and we can attach those results to the MA.

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v3.xlsx (pricing workbook), MA_proposal_Skyforge_v1.docx (master agreement draft)

Best,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
